solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Obsession? Iron this out

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: out here means disordered or put out of place, so the letters of this are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone so obsessed with tidiness they cannot stop pressing their clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is an excessive fixation, the same idea as an obsession.

clue.text: Universal suffrage originally brought down by buffoons

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something down moves it lower in the column, here to the bottom

parts.note: cosmic means relating to the whole universe

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of suffrage

explanation.surface: A political complaint that votes for all were defeated by clowns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought down' shifts the S of COSMIC, the first letter of 'suffrage', to the foot of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Comics are comedians or clowns, and buffoons are people who play the fool.

clue.text: Kindle with intricate true tale grips one — it's right to go in for easy reading

parts.note: to kindle a fire is to light it

indicators.note: intricate means involved or tangled, so the letters of true tale, with those for one and right, are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram's main fodder
the Roman numeral I is one, and grips says the tale holds it among its letters
R is the abbreviation for right, told to go in among the other letters

explanation.surface: An e-reader user chooses a complicated yarn, hoping it is the right choice for something undemanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kindle' looks like the Amazon e-reader but is the verb. 'grips' and 'to go in' only say that I and R join the TRUETALE letters before 'intricate' mixes all ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Light literature is fiction meant for entertainment rather than study, i.e. undemanding reading.

clue.text: Ask directions to get unexpected pleasure

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass directions
a treat is a pleasant surprise

explanation.surface: Asking the way and being rewarded with a pleasant surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or request earnestly, a stronger form of asking.

clue.text: Place for kippers and porridge?

parts.note: kippers are smoked herrings and porridge is oats, both breakfast foods; but a kipper is also one who kips, or sleeps, so it is a place to sleep and eat

explanation.surface: Asking where to get a traditional British breakfast of smoked fish and oats.
explanation.walkthrough: Kippers are smoked herrings, a British breakfast dish; 'kip' is British slang for sleep, so kippers are also sleepers. Porridge is boiled oats.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest house offering a bed for the night and a morning meal suits both sleepers and breakfast eaters.

clue.text: Pervert loves rip in bodice

indicators.note: to pervert is to twist or distort, so the letters of loves rip are turned into another order

explanation.surface: A lecherous man who enjoys tearing a woman's bodice.
explanation.definitionFit: An overslip is a loose garment worn over another, a kind of outer bodice or upper-body covering.

clue.text: Top of Brazil nut tree changes to dark brown

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter
changes means the letters of nut tree alter their order

explanation.surface: A Brazil nut tree's leaves turning brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut tree' seems one botanical unit with Brazil, but Brazil only lends its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunette describes hair or colouring of a deep brown shade.

clue.text: Protest turning into loss of status

parts.note: a demo is a protest march or demonstration

indicators.note: turning means the letters of into are spun round into a new order

explanation.surface: A protest that degenerates and costs its leaders their standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being demoted means being moved to a lower rank, a loss of standing.

clue.text: Around river little folk can be slippery young things

indicators.note: the little folk go around, enclosing, the river letter

parts.note: elves are small folk of legend

explanation.surface: Fairies by a riverbank can be slippery youngsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvers are young eels, slippery creatures in their early stage of life.

clue.text: Initially taxes are dropping a little bit

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: Taxes are starting to fall slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tad is informal for a small amount or slight degree.

clue.text: He perfects a knockout blow

definitions.meaning: one who puts the final touches to a piece of work
a decisive punch that ends a fight

explanation.surface: A boxer who has honed a decisive punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A finisher both completes work in a trade and is the final blow in a bout.

clue.text: One gets call after a short trip out

indicators.note: after places the pieces for one and call behind the letter a

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone receives a phone call just after a brief outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link word joining I and RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking someone or something for an airing means a brief excursion outdoors.

clue.text: Del flaunts outrageously wearing white suit

indicators.note: the word white wears the rearranged letters, holding them inside it

parts.note: taken as the word itself

indicators.note: outrageously suggests wild behaviour, so the letters of Del flaunts are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Del Boy showing off in a flashy white suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Del Boy is the flashy wheeler-dealer of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses; the answer is Cockney rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang the phrase rhymes with, and stands for, a set of matching clothes.

clue.text: Little devil! He's regularly into mum's port

indicators.note: regularly picks letters at a steady interval, here every fourth letter of the closing words

explanation.surface: A naughty child caught raiding the drinks cabinet for mother's port.
explanation.walkthrough: Every fourth letter of INTOMUMSPORT, starting with the first, gives I, M and P; 'He's' is a link meaning the answer is found there.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a small demon, and by extension a mischievous child.

clue.text: Spanish grass, leaving Spain, operates on the run

indicators.note: on the run suggests flight and disorder, so the remaining letters are scattered into a new order
leaving says the letter for Spain departs from the word operates

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Spanish turf that, with Spain gone, works while on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes E from OPERATES, leaving OPRATES, which 'on the run' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough grass of Spain and North Africa used for rope and paper.

clue.text: Post bestowed upon minor lacking in craft?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece is set upon, or above, the second

parts.note: to ship goods is to send or post them
minor and less both mean smaller or lesser

explanation.surface: A job given to a youngster with no skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like skill but means boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no vessels means being without craft in the nautical sense, a punning definition.

clue.text: Literally, when abbreviated, sales information's worthless

indicators.note: abbreviated means shortened, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an advert is information meant to promote sales
bum is slang for worthless or useless

explanation.surface: A cynic says sales literature is worthless when cut down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when abbreviated' trims ADVERT to ADVER; ''s' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad verbum is Latin for word for word, meaning to the letter.

clue.text: Mini-outing for English literature form?

definitions.meaning: a small journey: a trip with the diminutive ending -let
a group of three rhyming lines in verse

explanation.surface: A short school trip arranged for an English literature class.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a playful coinage: -let makes small things (piglet), so a little trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tercet of three rhyming lines is a poetic form, and a tiny trip is a joking sense.

clue.text: Garland regularly on display in Algeria

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of Algeria, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Floral garlands routinely shown in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian wreath of flowers worn around the neck.

clue.text: Dancing sprites linger in the mind

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so sprites is rearranged

explanation.surface: Fairy figures dancing stay in one's memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory that persists continues to remain, staying with someone.

clue.text: Runner-up lives out wild dream still

indicators.note: out and wild both describe letters gone astray, so these three words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: An athlete who finished second still lives out a crazy dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Second place in a contest earns silver, so the second finisher is a silver medal winner.

clue.text: Note: Girlfriend loses nothing becoming member of police force

parts.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: loses says the letter for nothing is taken out of the girlfriend word

parts.note: woman is used informally for a girlfriend or partner
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A girlfriend gives up everything to join the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes O from WOMAN, leaving WMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawman is an officer of the law, such as a sheriff or police officer.

clue.text: Could be crook series is cut short before end of episode

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter of the word for series is removed

parts.note: a string is a series, as in a string of wins

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of episode

explanation.surface: A TV crime series axed just before the finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal, but in Australian slang it means ill or broken. Strine is a humorous name for Australian English.
explanation.definitionFit: Crook, meaning unwell, is an example of Australian vernacular speech.

clue.text: Red mark of omission circles line

indicators.note: circles means the mark goes round the letter for line

parts.note: a caret is the proofreading mark showing where something is to be inserted

explanation.surface: A red editing mark ringing a line of text.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is a red wine from Bordeaux, and the deep red colour named after it.

clue.text: Sort a few corrupt computer programs

indicators.note: corrupt data is scrambled, so the letters of sort a few are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sorting out a few corrupted computer files.
explanation.definitionFit: Software is the collective term for programs that run on a computer.

clue.text: A Parisian institute or Oxford maybe

parts.note: un is French for a

explanation.surface: A French institution, or perhaps an Oxford one.
explanation.definitionFit: Uni is informal for university, and Oxford is one example.

clue.text: Publisher is certain to reverse final entries

indicators.note: the last two letters of the word for certain swap their order

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A publisher who is sure to overturn the last items accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse final entries' swaps the last two letters of SURE to give SUER.
explanation.definitionFit: An issuer is one who issues or puts out something, as a publisher does.

clue.text: Supports South American volunteers in Sweden

parts.note: US means American
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Backing for American volunteers in Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to hold it up or keep it going, as a support does.
